title: Homogenization, multiscale FEM and heterogeneous media

items.title: Uniformly elliptic periodic scalar diffusion data
items.statement: Fix a measurable scalar coefficient a that is Z^d-periodic and satisfies 0<lambda<=a<=Lambda almost everywhere; set A_epsilon(x)=a(x/epsilon)I on the unit cube with homogeneous Dirichlet data.
items.strategy: State the coefficient, cell, period, energy form, and weak boundary-value branch.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.1, PDF pp. 1–3: periodic scalar conductivity, unit cell, ellipticity and zero-Dirichlet model.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.1–1.3, printed pp. 3–23: bounded periodic coefficients and Dirichlet homogenization setting.

items.title: Zero-mean periodic Sobolev cell space
items.statement: Define the H1 periodic closure on Y=(0,1)^d and its closed zero-mean subspace, with gradients and normalized cell integrals.
items.strategy: Fix equivalence-class and periodic-trace conventions, mean normalization, and the Hilbert norm.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §§1.2.2–1.2.3, PDF pp. 6–8: periodic cell space, corrector mean convention and variational formulation.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.1–1.2, printed pp. 3–13: periodic Sobolev corrector space and cell normalization.

items.title: Periodic scalar cell problem
items.statement: For each macroscopic vector p define the weak periodic cell equation for a mean-zero corrector chi_p, without asserting existence in the definition.
items.strategy: Specify the test space, coefficient, sign convention, and mean-zero gauge.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.2.3, PDF pp. 7–8: the variational cell problem and mean-zero corrector.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–13: periodic corrector equations.

items.title: Mean-zero Poincare inequality on the periodic cell
items.statement: On the unit cell, each mean-zero periodic H1 function obeys ||v||L2<=sqrt(d)||grad v||L2, and every periodic H1 gradient has zero cell mean.
items.strategy: Prove the zero mean of smooth periodic derivatives on opposite faces, then prove Poincare by coordinate telescoping, Jensen, Fubini, and Cauchy-Schwarz; pass both claims to the closure.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.2.2, PDF pp. 6–7: Poincare inequality on the periodic mean-zero space.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–13: coercivity on periodic corrector spaces.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of periodic cell correctors
items.statement: For every p in R^d the cell equation has a unique mean-zero solution chi_p, linear in p, with an energy bound depending only on lambda and Lambda.
items.strategy: Use the cell Poincare bound to make the gradient norm Hilbert-equivalent and apply Lax-Milgram.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.2.3, PDF pp. 7–8: Lax–Milgram solution and energy estimate for cell correctors.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–13: existence, uniqueness and bounds for periodic correctors.

items.title: Periodic correctors and effective tensor
items.statement: Use the unique coordinate correctors to define chi_p and A* p=integral_Y a(p+grad chi_p).
items.strategy: State the coordinate and flux-average conventions; well-definedness is supplied by the cited cell-solvability lemma.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.2.3, PDF pp. 7–8: effective matrix defined by averaged corrector flux.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.2–1.3, printed pp. 9–23: correctors and homogenized coefficient.

items.title: Symmetry and uniform ellipticity of the effective tensor
items.statement: For scalar a with lambda<=a<=Lambda, A* is symmetric and lambda I<=A*<=Lambda I.
items.strategy: Use the cell equation for the symmetric energy representation, mean-zero gradients, and the minimizing characterization.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.2.3, PDF pp. 7–9: symmetric energy formula and ellipticity of the effective matrix.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–13: symmetry and uniform ellipticity of the homogenized matrix.

items.title: Periodic averaging and rescaling bounds on the unit cube
items.statement: For periodic L1 data and compactly supported smooth slow factors, cell rescaling converges to the cell mean; periodic L2 rescalings have a uniform L2 bound on the unit cube.
items.strategy: Tile the support by epsilon-cells, compare the slow factor on each cell, bound the boundary-cell remainder, and extend the weak limit by L2 density.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: Lemma 1.3.2 and its proof, PDF pp. 12–13: periodic averaging on bounded sets.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 14–19: periodic oscillations and weak averaging.

items.title: Two-scale weak convergence for periodic tests
items.statement: Define two-scale convergence of bounded L2 sequences by testing against finite sums phi(x)psi(y), compactly supported in the slow variable and smooth periodic in y.
items.strategy: Fix the Y-periodic test convention and the limiting pairing on the product space.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: Definition 1.3.3, PDF p. 13: two-scale convergence on periodic test functions.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 14–19: periodic two-scale limits.

items.title: Two-scale compactness for bounded L2 sequences
items.statement: Every sequence bounded in L2((0,1)^d) has a subsequence two-scale convergent to a function in L2((0,1)^d x Y).
items.strategy: Use the periodic sampling norm identity, a countable dense product-test family, deterministic diagonal extraction, and Riesz representation.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: Theorem 1.3.4 and proof, PDF pp. 13–15: two-scale compactness by a countable test family and Riesz representation.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 14–20: two-scale compactness theorem and proof.

items.title: Separable H1-zero space and compact L2 inclusion on a cube
items.statement: For the unit cube, H1-zero is a separable Hilbert space, satisfies a choice-free coordinate Poincare bound under countable choice, and is compactly embedded in L2 by Fourier-tail control.
items.strategy: Embed in a finite product of separable L2 spaces, prove Poincare on test functions, and use periodic Fourier coefficients of zero extensions with a uniform high-frequency tail bound.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.1, printed pp. 3–8: H1-zero energy space, Poincaré control and bounded-solution compactness context.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.3.1, PDF pp. 11–14: uniform H1-zero bounds and the compact L2 subsequence used in homogenization.

items.title: Two-scale structure of bounded H1-zero gradients
items.statement: A bounded H1-zero sequence on the cube has a subsequence with u_n weakly H1 to u and grad u_n two-scale convergent to grad u+grad_y u1, with u1 mean-zero periodic H1 in y.
items.strategy: Show the two-scale limit of u_n is y-independent, test gradients against y-divergence-free fields, and construct the unique mean-zero potential by Fourier coefficients.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: Theorem 1.3.6 and proof, PDF pp. 14–16: two-scale limits of bounded gradients are gradient plus a periodic potential.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 18–23: gradient decomposition in periodic homogenization.

items.title: Periodic scalar Dirichlet homogenization on the unit cube
items.statement: For every bounded periodic scalar coefficient a and f in L2 on the unit cube, the exact H1-zero solutions converge weakly to the unique solution with coefficient A*.
items.strategy: Obtain the two-scale gradient limit, identify the cell equation using epsilon-scaled oscillating tests, average the flux, and use uniqueness to remove subsequences.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.3.1, PDF pp. 11–16: oscillating-test proof of periodic homogenization.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 14–23: two-scale compactness, cell identification, and homogenized equation.

items.title: Strong L2 convergence in periodic Dirichlet homogenization
items.statement: The periodic Dirichlet solutions from the preceding theorem converge strongly in L2 to the homogenized solution.
items.strategy: Apply the local cube compactness lemma to every parameter sequence and identify every strong cluster limit by the weak homogenization theorem.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.3.1, PDF pp. 11–16: compactness upgrades weak homogenization to strong L2 convergence.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 14–23: compactness of solutions and uniqueness of the homogenized limit.

items.title: Antisymmetric periodic flux potential
items.statement: Each mean-zero divergence-free periodic corrector flux has an L2 antisymmetric potential whose periodic divergence is the flux and whose norm is bounded by the flux L2 norm.
items.strategy: Solve a mean-zero periodic Poisson problem by Lax-Milgram; prove the vector-potential divergence vanishes by Fourier coefficients.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.3.1, PDF pp. 15–16: periodic flux potentials in corrector estimates.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 35–45: flux correctors and antisymmetric potentials.

items.title: Boundary-cutoff corrector estimate for regular periodic data
items.statement: If the cell corrector gradients are bounded and u0 is C2 on the closed cube, a boundary-cutoff first-order corrector approximates u_epsilon in H1 seminorm within C sqrt(epsilon), and u_epsilon-u0 is O(sqrt(epsilon)) in L2.
items.strategy: Construct the cutoff expansion, bound its boundary-strip residual, use the antisymmetric flux potential to gain epsilon in the interior, and test the residual equation with the error.

sources.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
sources.locator: §1.3.1, PDF pp. 15–16: boundary-cutoff first-order corrector and square-root energy rate.

sources.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §2.2, printed pp. 40–45: flux-corrector residual and boundary-layer cutoff estimate.

items.title: Periodic FE-HMM with simplicial macro and periodic P1 micro meshes
items.statement: Define a finite FE-HMM procedure using an admissible 2D NVB macro triangulation, conforming zero-boundary P1 macro space, positive quadrature, periodized micro sampling domains, periodic P1 cell meshes, and the resulting macro solve.
items.strategy: Specify every input, sampling domain, coupling convention, matrix formula, finite solve, and singular-system output.

sources.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
sources.locator: §§2–3: quadrature points, periodic cell sampling, and macro assembly conventions.

items.title: Well-posedness of the finite FE-HMM micro solves
items.statement: Each periodic finite-dimensional P1 micro cell problem in the FE-HMM algorithm has a unique zero-mean solution for every input gradient.
items.strategy: Restrict the uniformly elliptic form to the finite periodic subspace and apply Lax-Milgram.

sources.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
sources.locator: §§2–3: FE-HMM quadrature samples, periodic micro coupling and macro assembly.

items.title: Energy identity for FE-HMM micro tensor error
items.statement: The discrete cell energy exceeds the exact sampled tensor energy by the squared coefficient-weighted gradient error, giving a bound by the best micro-space approximation of the exact corrector.
items.strategy: Subtract the continuous and discrete variational equations and use the energy-minimizing characterization.

sources.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
sources.locator: §§2–3: cell sampling and the FE-HMM macro/micro error split.

items.title: No sampling resonance for period-aligned periodic micro cells
items.statement: If the micro sample length is an integer multiple of epsilon and is aligned to a periodic cell phase, the exact periodic-coupling sampled tensor equals A* in every dimension.
items.strategy: Pull the corrector back by the integer dilation, verify its weak cell equation, and average the periodic flux over the integer number of cells.

sources.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
sources.locator: §§2–3: periodic micro problems and FE-HMM assembly conventions.

items.title: One-dimensional nonaligned micro sampling resonance bound
items.statement: For one-dimensional scalar periodic data and periodic coupling on a sample ratio r=delta/epsilon>=1, the exact sampled harmonic tensor differs from A* by at most 2 Lambda^2/lambda times epsilon/delta.
items.strategy: Use the harmonic-mean cell formula, split the interval into whole periods and one remainder, then compare reciprocal averages.

sources.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
sources.locator: §§2–3: micro sampling domains, coupling conditions, and effective coefficient reconstruction.

items.title: FE-HMM macro, micro, and sampling error separation
items.statement: If the total micro-plus-sampling tensor discrepancy is below lambda, the FE-HMM macro solution exists uniquely and its energy error is bounded by the best macro approximation plus explicit micro and resonance terms.
items.strategy: Bound the bilinear-form perturbation by the tensor discrepancy, prove coercivity, and derive a finite-dimensional energy-Strang estimate.

sources.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
sources.locator: §3: discrete macro problem, sampled effective matrices, and micro/macro error terms.

title: Homogenization, multiscale FEM and heterogeneous media — Examples

items.title: Layered medium: harmonic normal and arithmetic tangential means
items.statement: For a two-phase coefficient layered in y1, compute the exact diagonal effective tensor and verify the harmonic/arithmetic directions.
items.strategy: Solve the one-dimensional normal flux equation and test the tangential cell equation directly.

items.title: High contrast destroys contrast-independent conditioning
items.statement: For a layered coefficient taking values kappa and 1 on equal fractions, compute the condition number of A* and show it diverges as kappa decreases to zero.
items.strategy: Use the exact layered tensor from the cell formulas and compute its two eigenvalues.

items.title: FE-HMM energy error ledger with distinct components
items.statement: Substitute exact rational macro, micro, resonance, ellipticity, and solution-norm values into the proven FE-HMM error bound.
items.strategy: Compute the discrepancy threshold, coercivity factor, and each error contribution exactly.

items.title: A nonaligned one-dimensional micro window has resonance error
items.statement: Compute the exact sampled and homogenized harmonic means for a two-phase periodic coefficient at delta/epsilon=3/2 and verify the resonance bound.
items.strategy: Integrate the reciprocal coefficient over one and one-half periods and compare the two reciprocal averages.
